verifications.note: OG&E application to ODEQ for River Valley Generating Station, Le Flore County. It proposes five GE 7F.05 gas simple-cycle turbines of about 224.8 MW each, about 1,124 MW, or two combined-cycle blocks, to replace the coal units.

records.action: Add one new gas unit group of five simple-cycle turbines at the existing River Valley plant, pre-construction.
records.note: GEM lists only the two coal units here. OG&E applied to ODEQ for a construction permit, number 2025-0187, to install five GE 7F.05 gas turbines of about 224.8 MW each, about 1,124 MW in total, while retiring the coal units. A second option in the same application is two combined-cycle blocks of about 1,280 MW. The Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2024-286 for 496 MW at the nearby 161 kV substation is a smaller figure than the permit, so the permit capacity is used and the mismatch is flagged in a question. The new unit is named 3 because GEM already lists units 1 and 2. The five turbines are one unit group of five engines. The owner is Oklahoma Gas and Electric, the applicant on the permit, and it already owns units 1 and 2.

verifications.note: SPP surplus study report for GEN-2025-SR9. It describes 20 INDAR and Ingeteam synchronous gas-fired units of 21.0812 MW each, 421.6 MW in all at the Muskogee 345 kilovolt substation, shared with Muskogee units 4, 5 and 6 (1,908 MW), limited to 400 MW of injection.

records.note: GEM has the plant but not this unit. SPP's surplus interconnection study for GEN-2025-SR9 describes 20 INDAR and Ingeteam synchronous gas-fired units of 21.0812 MW each, 421.6 MW in all, connecting at the Muskogee 345 kilovolt substation, shared with Muskogee units 4, 5 and 6 (1,908 MW). The queue row reads: Fort Gibson, OG&E area, 400 MW, IA PENDING, commercial operation December 1, 2029. The injection is capped at 400 MW, but the equipment adds up to more, and the listed capacity is the equipment total. The interconnection agreement is still pending, so the status is announced. SPP does not publish the name of the company behind a queue request, and no regulator filing or news item naming it was found, so the owner is left blank for the reviewer. OG&E owns the existing units at this point, but a surplus request can come from a different company, so no owner is assumed. The study says synchronous gas-fired units without naming the engine maker's model, so the engine type is read from the unit size and count.

records.researcher_notes: The Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority applied to the state environmental agency in May 2026 for a construction permit for one new 90 megawatt General Electric 7E.03 simple cycle natural gas turbine at its Lamb plant in Ponca City. The state agency's completeness letter is dated June 8, 2026, and a notice of filing for New Unit 2 ran in the Ponca City News on June 11, 2026. The application gives 2028 as the construction date, so 2028 is used as the start year. A Southwest Power Pool request matched to this plant shows 103 to 124 megawatts, which is likely a winter or study rating. The permit application figure is the manufacturer nameplate figure used here. The permit is still in technical review, so the status stays pre-construction until a permit is issued and work starts.
